evals.prompt: This settings card feels flat and slightly misaligned; polish it.
evals.expected_behavior: Inspects the current UI, styles, and shared design-system primitives/tokens before proposing any changes, separates structural issues from polish issues, then proposes concrete component-level diffs grouped by principle.
assertions: Inspects existing component code/tokens before proposing changes, not before-the-fact guesses
Groups proposed changes by principle (typography, surfaces, motion, etc.) rather than a flat list
Uses existing design tokens/utilities rather than inventing new values

evals.prompt: Add a smooth expand/collapse animation to this accordion item using whatever motion tooling is best.
evals.expected_behavior: Checks whether `motion`/`framer-motion` is already a dependency before reaching for it; if not present, uses CSS/native transitions instead of adding a new animation library just for this interaction, and avoids `transition: all`.
assertions: Checks package.json for an existing motion library before recommending one
Does not add a new motion dependency purely for this transition when CSS transitions would do
Does not use `transition: all` or `will-change: all`
deterministic_checks: confirms whether `motion` or `framer-motion` is already a dependency before recommending motion-based patterns

evals.prompt: Review this dashboard component for polish issues and give me a report, not code changes yet.
evals.expected_behavior: Produces a review grouped by principle using a markdown table with Before and After columns, cites the file/selector/component for each finding, and omits categories that were reviewed but needed no changes rather than padding the report.
assertions: Groups findings by principle with a markdown table using Before and After columns
Cites the file, selector, or component for each finding
Omits reviewed categories that needed no changes rather than padding the report

evals.prompt: Make this modal screen-reader accessible and fix keyboard focus traps.
evals.expected_behavior: Does not treat accessibility compliance as visual feel polish; handles it directly as an accessibility task or routes to a more appropriate specialist.
assertions: Acknowledges accessibility is the primary task
Does not focus on radius/shadows/motion as the main solution

evals.prompt: Design a brand-new settings page layout from scratch; nothing exists yet to react to.
evals.expected_behavior: Declines to apply polish-focused guidance since there is no existing UI to refine, and treats this as net-new product/IA design work, which is out of this skill's scope.
assertions: Does not propose radius/shadow/motion polish changes with no existing UI to react to
States this is net-new design/IA work rather than interface-feel polish
